questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Lisbon because I had never been in Portugal before and I wanted to experience the country and meet the Portuguese people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I find the application proces to be easy. The University of Lisbon send me several information e-mail before arrival so I wasn't in any doubt at any time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not recieve any assistance, I just took a taxi to my place of accomondation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I joined a couple of Facebook groups where I got advice on housing. This helped me find the different housing companies so I was sure I wouldn't get scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That accomondation is very very expensive in Lisbon. I paid 900 euros each month for a tiny room in a shared apartment with 11 other exchange students. I also paid a lot of different fees. Unfortunately, we also had some issues with our landlords, who didn't provide any service at all including not fixing the things that were broken. But i heard that other people had better experiences with landlords. 

However, Lisbon is easy to get around by public transport, so I would recommend living off campus because the universities are not located in the city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We got an email about enrolment for the courses and that it would open on a certain date and time, but I was at work at the time, so when I finally - a few hours later - went to sign up for the courses I wanted, there weren't many available. On top of that, you had to check if these courses overlapped on the schedule, but I think it worked fine. 

There was also a lack of transparency around the fact that once you hit submit, you couldn't do it again. This stressed me out as I had chosen a course that I definitely didn't want, so I had to email the host university back and forth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide on e-mail and then just e-mail, they didn't pick up the phone at the host University.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As I said, I was late, and it was first come, first served, so I wasn't that succesful, but everything were fine in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when registration opens if it's first come, first served.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We were adviced by our sending University (UCPH) that we should apply for master courses because the level were often low on bachelor courses in Lisbon, so I took both. But to be honest, the level were low on all my courses, it was comparable to high school first year in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most classes weren't as structured and teachers would just ask students what they thought instead of teaching themselves. The lectures where the teachers were prepared, the level of what was presented was unfortunately very low.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Statistical Indicators, Field Research, Inquiry Methods Online, Contemporary Social Inequalities, Portuguese History and Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Portuguese History and Culture. Even though I am a social scientist and the subject is humanities, I thought it was perfect to learn about the country you were in, its history, people, culture, etc. It gave some great insights. And also the teacher were the best I had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really unexpected. Just remember to save up money for travels.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was definitely more expensive than expected. Also because many companies want you to pay for at least 6 month, and for many people, a study exchange is about 5 months, so you need to pay for a month when you don't even live there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join anything, så I can't answer that question.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't join anything, så I can't answer that question.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There are some organisations that organise a lot of activities in collaboration with Erasmus. These can be good to participate in during the first weeks, there were various trips to the Belom area, Sintra, and party-related activities such as Pub Crawl and Boat Party. After the first few weeks, however, I sought out more local social activities, I went to cross fit, joined a gym and went to football training with international teams. I found these on my own. 

In my time I also went to many Benfica and Sporting matches. Also champions league and europe league.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend them to go to the beaches, to Sintra, to the Algarve coast, to maderia, to the Azores, to Porto. Plan some trips with other exchange students, I went there with my roomies.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, the Portuguese are very nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's easy to feel lonely in a foreign country at first, so I highly recommend finding shared accommodation with other exchange students. It was the best decision I made. That way I didn't have to look for other people at my school as much because there were 12 of us at home having fun together. We played padel together, went on runs, travelled, had Christmas parties, went out, etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It challenged my patience that it was so difficult to find the items you needed in the supermarket and that you queue a lot in Portugal. There were also quite a few men who would whistle at you or say something to you on the street, presumably because you were Nordic-looking with blonde hair. But you just have to ignore that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, the friendliness. The good restaurants and bars.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to look for acommondation well in advance so you can find something cheaper that I did. And be realistic, you will not find anything under 700 euros.

Remember good shoes for walking. The city is very hilly and there are cobblestones all over, it is very slippery when it rains. 

Enjoy the beaches during the summer period.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The academic level is lower than UCPH, so don't choose this destination for academic reasons.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, the experience from living in a foreign country, the improvement of my English language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having a packed weekly calendar. I'm used to juggling sports, full-time study, part-time work and social life. And often in Lisbon, I had to find things to fill my days myself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
